actions.action: Trim basil stems back about one-third, cutting just above a set of side shoots/leaf buds
Separate store-bought basil into individual plants
Prune/harvest basil every two weeks or so during summer
Apply liquid organic fertilizer such as fish emulsion after a big harvest
Check weekly for flower buds and pinch them off
Shear flowers off Greek basil with snips or shears
Optionally buy herb snips for cutting
Grow a slow-bolting or sterile variety such as Everleaf, Emerald Towers or Pesto Perpetuo

verdict.reason: The answer is a generic scraped article on trimming basil that never actually diagnoses an overgrown, woody plant. Its main advice, cutting above side shoots to make the plant bushier, still matches the fix that worked, and nothing in it is harmful.
